question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The codebase can already fix narrow FreeBSD bugs, but official OS support changes docs, installers, service lifecycle, release validation, and long-term ownership commitments.

options.title: Define Community FreeBSD Scope
options.body: Keep the issue open and document FreeBSD as community or experimental only if maintainers want to acknowledge external packaging without owning Tier 1 release support.

options.title: Promote Toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD ownership and open tracked implementation work for installer/update behavior, service management, docs, CI, and release validation.

options.title: Decline Official Support
options.body: Close this as not planned if maintainers decide FreeBSD ports/pkg should remain external and unsupported by OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Define Community FreeBSD Scope
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and document FreeBSD as community or experimental only if maintainers want to acknowledge external packaging without owning Tier 1 release support.

likelyOwner.reason: The core question is the product support contract and long-term platform ownership, which routes to the project lead listed in CONTRIBUTING.md.
